bullets: Alert fatigue stems from signal-to-noise imbalance, not human failure — the system generates too many alerts, not the team's fault.
Noise in alerts undermines trust, making real incidents harder to detect — even critical alerts risk being ignored.
The key metric is actionability: if fewer than half of all alerts lead to meaningful action, the system has a noise problem.
Tuning alerts before training humans is essential — improving the signal is more effective than demanding better discipline.
Real incidents are often missed not because of poor response, but because of overexposure to irrelevant alerts.
A well-tuned alert system ensures that every page has a purpose — if it doesn't, it's noise.
The goal is not to increase willpower but to reduce the number of false or low-value alerts.
When alerts are reliable, teams respond to them — when they aren't, they don’t.
